notYet: Not yet part of the eastern Mediterranean

stages.name: Contested
stages.desc: Fought over by Athens, Sparta and Persia

stages.name: Athenian-held
stages.desc: Led by Athens and its maritime empire

stages.name: Spartan-held
stages.desc: Led by Sparta and its allies

stages.name: Persian
stages.desc: Ruled by the Great King, his satraps and vassal kings

states.name: Cyprus
timeline: City-kingdoms, Greek and Phoenician, under the Persian king
About this year Evagoras seizes Salamis from its Phoenician ruler, as a vassal of Persia
Conon finds refuge with Evagoras after Aegospotami

states.name: Israel
timeline: Persian provinces inland; Phoenician-run ports along the coast
Diodorus says Egyptian and Arabian kings had designs on the Phoenician coast
As Egypt breaks away, this coast becomes Persia's southern frontier

states.name: Lebanon
timeline: Sidon, Tyre and their neighbours: vassal kings who provide the core of the Persian navy
A royal fleet is manned for the Aegean, stops at Aspendus and comes home unused

states.name: Syria
timeline: Part of the Persian province called Beyond the River; Arwad sends ships to the King
Arwad, off this coast, is one of the Phoenician cities that owe the King ships

states.name: Turkey
timeline: Persian satraps rule the interior, the largest part; Greek cities on the coast pay tribute to Athens
Miletus and other coastal cities revolt; Sparta and Tissaphernes sign their first treaty
A third treaty promises the King's ships; a Phoenician fleet reaches Aspendus and goes no further
Thrasyllus lands at Ephesus and is beaten off with the satrap's help
Athens wins back Chalcedon and Byzantium on the Bosporus
Prince Cyrus arrives at Sardis and pays Sparta's crews
Aegospotami, on the Hellespont, destroys the last Athenian fleet
By treaty the Greek cities of Asia are the King's, though Spartan governors sit in some of them

states.name: Greece
timeline: Athens' Aegean empire still stands, but Sparta leads the Peloponnese and has fortified Decelea, and the fleet is lost in Sicily
Chios and other allies revolt, and a Spartan fleet enters the Aegean
The Four Hundred seize power in Athens; Euboea revolts
Victory at Cyzicus revives Athens, and full democracy is restored
Alcibiades returns to Athens; Lysander takes over the Spartan fleet
Athens wins at Arginusae, then executes six of its generals
After Aegospotami the empire surrenders city by city; Samos and besieged Athens hold out
Athens surrenders, its Long Walls are pulled down and the Thirty are installed

events.title: Decelea fortified
events.text: King Agis of Sparta occupies Decelea in the spring, cutting Athens off from its farmland all year round.

events.title: Athens builds again
events.text: With its best ships gone, Athens gathers timber and money for a new fleet that winter.

events.title: The King wants tribute
events.text: Darius II presses Tissaphernes, satrap at Sardis, for tribute from the Greek cities of the coast.

events.title: News from Sicily
events.text: In September Athens' expedition to Syracuse is wiped out, with some two hundred warships lost.

events.title: Samos stays loyal
events.text: A popular rising keeps Samos on Athens' side, and it becomes the main Athenian naval base.

events.title: Iasus stormed
events.text: The Peloponnesians take Iasus and hand the King's rebel Amorges to Tissaphernes.

events.title: Alcibiades changes sides
events.text: Distrusted by Sparta, the Athenian exile Alcibiades moves to the court of Tissaphernes.

events.title: Chios revolts
events.text: Chios, Athens' strongest remaining naval ally, goes over to Sparta.

events.title: Miletus revolts
events.text: Miletus follows Chios and becomes the base of the Spartan fleet in Ionia.

events.title: First treaty
events.text: Sparta recognises the King's claim to every city his ancestors held, in return for support.

events.title: The Four Hundred
events.text: Oligarchs overthrow the democracy in Athens; the fleet at Samos refuses to follow them.

events.title: Third treaty
events.text: In the plain of the Maeander, Tissaphernes promises pay until the King's ships arrive.

events.title: Evagoras takes Salamis
events.text: About this year Evagoras seizes Salamis in Cyprus from its Phoenician ruler.

events.title: Euboea revolts
events.text: A Spartan squadron beats the Athenians off Eretria, and most of Euboea changes sides.

events.title: Battle of Cynossema
events.text: Mindarus gives up on the Phoenicians and sails to the Hellespont, where Athens beats him.

events.title: Threat to Phoenicia?
events.text: Diodorus says the fleet went home because Egyptian and Arabian kings had designs on Phoenicia.

events.title: Alcibiades at Phaselis
events.text: With thirteen ships he sails for Aspendus, and returns claiming to have kept the fleet from Sparta.

events.title: Ships from Phoenicia
events.text: Phoenician cities man a royal fleet to fight beside the Spartans in the Aegean.

events.title: 147 ships at Aspendus
events.text: A hundred and forty-seven Phoenician warships reach Aspendus, and come no further.

events.title: Democracy restored
events.text: After Cyzicus, full democracy returns to Athens.

events.title: Battle of Cyzicus
events.text: Athens captures or destroys the whole Spartan fleet, and Mindarus is killed.

events.title: Pylos falls
events.text: Sparta recovers Pylos, which Athens had held since 425 BC.

events.title: Thrasyllus at Ephesus
events.text: An Athenian landing at Ephesus is beaten off by the city and Tissaphernes' troops.

events.title: Chalcedon submits
events.text: Athens brings Chalcedon to terms at the mouth of the Black Sea.

events.title: Byzantium regained
events.text: Athens takes Byzantium back and reopens the grain route.

events.title: Alcibiades returns
events.text: Alcibiades comes home to Athens in triumph and is given supreme command.

events.title: Cyrus arrives
events.text: Darius sends his younger son Cyrus to Sardis with five hundred talents for Sparta's war.

events.title: One more obol
events.text: At Lysander's request Cyrus raises the Spartan rowers' pay from three obols a day to four.

events.title: Battle of Notium
events.text: Lysander beats Alcibiades' deputy, and Alcibiades goes into exile for good.

events.title: Cyrus's closed door
events.text: Cyrus keeps the new Spartan admiral, Callicratidas, waiting for money.

events.title: Conon trapped
events.text: Callicratidas blockades the Athenian general Conon in the harbour of Mytilene.

events.title: Generals executed
events.text: Athens puts six victorious generals to death for failing to rescue shipwrecked crews.

events.title: Battle of Arginusae
events.text: Athens wins a huge sea battle near Lesbos, and Callicratidas is drowned.

events.title: Cyrus's treasury
events.text: Called to his dying father, Cyrus leaves Lysander his money and his cities' tribute.

events.title: Conon flees to Cyprus
events.text: Conon escapes with a few ships and takes refuge with Evagoras of Salamis.

events.title: Byzantium surrenders
events.text: Byzantium and Chalcedon open their gates to Lysander.

events.title: Athens besieged
events.text: Lysander blockades Piraeus while two Spartan kings camp outside the walls.

events.title: Battle of Aegospotami
events.text: Lysander captures almost the entire Athenian fleet on the beach.

events.title: Egypt breaks away
events.text: Amyrtaeus of Sais ends Persian rule in the Nile Delta.

events.title: Samos surrenders
events.text: Athens' last loyal ally gives in to Lysander.

events.title: Death of Darius
events.text: King Darius II dies and his elder son takes the throne as Artaxerxes II.

events.title: Athens surrenders
events.text: Starved out, Athens gives up its empire, its walls and all but twelve ships.

chartNote: Share of the area of six present-day countries, each coloured as a single region: a deliberate simplification using today's boundaries. Greece is shown as Athenian-held in 413 BC because the Aegean empire still stood, although Sparta led the Peloponnese and much of the north was independent. Turkey is shown as contested from 412 to 405 BC because its coast and straits were fought over; its interior stayed Persian throughout.
